content.text: {"primary_meaning": "Divine blessing and favor — God's quiet, life-giving, refreshing grace descending on His people, often tied to fertility, provision, and prosperity.", "primary_basis": ["Genesis 27:28 (Isaac's blessing: 'God give thee of the dew of heaven')", "Deuteronomy 33:13, 28 (blessing of dew on Israel)", "Hosea 14:5 ('I will be as the dew unto Israel')", "Psalm 133:3 ('as the dew of Hermon... there the LORD commanded the blessing')", "Proverbs 19:12 (the king's favor 'is as dew upon the grass')", "Micah 5:7 (the remnant of Jacob 'as a dew from the LORD')", "Zechariah 8:12 and Haggai 1:10 (dew given or withheld as sign of blessing or judgment)"], "alternatives": [{"meaning": "God's word, teaching, or doctrine gently distilling on hearers", "basis": ["Deuteronomy 32:2 ('my speech shall distil as the dew')"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "Transience and fleetingness — that which quickly evaporates, used of Israel's inconstant devotion or of the wicked", "basis": ["Hosea 6:4 ('your goodness is as a morning cloud, and as the early dew it goeth away')", "Hosea 13:3"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "Resurrection and revivification of the dead", "basis": ["Isaiah 26:19 ('thy dew is as the dew of herbs, and the earth shall cast out the dead'; also rabbinic 'dew of resurrection' tradition carried into some Christian exegesis)"], "prominence": "minority"}, {"meaning": "God's providential provision, associated with the manna", "basis": ["Exodus 16:13-14", "Numbers 11:9"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "The Holy Spirit or the Incarnation descending silently — patristic and Catholic typology, especially reading Gideon's fleece as a figure of Mary receiving Christ like dew", "basis": ["Judges 6:36-40", "Psalm 72:6 ('like showers that water the earth'; cf. Vulgate/liturgical 'Rorate caeli' from Isaiah 45:8)"], "prominence": "minority"}, {"meaning": "Youthful vigor, freshness, or the abundance of the Messiah's people/army", "basis": ["Psalm 110:3 ('thou hast the dew of thy youth')", "2 Samuel 17:12 (troops falling on the enemy 'as the dew falleth on the ground')"], "prominence": "minority"}], "has_settled_consensus": true, "confidence": "high", "notes": "There is a broadly recognizable consensus that dew primarily symbolizes divine blessing, favor, and refreshing grace, rooted in its role in the arid Near East as an essential, silently arriving source of moisture. However, dew is a polyvalent image in Scripture: the same figure is also used negatively for transience (Hosea) and positively for resurrection, provision, and teaching. Commentators (e.g., Matthew Henry, Keil-Delitzsch, standard Bible dictionaries such as ISBE and the Dictionary of Biblical Imagery) generally treat blessing/grace as the leading sense while acknowledging the transience motif as a distinct secondary use. The Marian/incarnational reading of Gideon's fleece is well established in Catholic and Orthodox liturgical tradition but is not the dominant sense in Protestant exegesis."}
